What would bulk triage do, without doing it

Source: R/triage.R
triage_preview.Rd

A bulk write across a whole project is the highest-blast-radius action in the app, so it is never applied without showing the count first – including how many samples would end up with NOTHING kept, which is the outcome that silently loses a sample.

Usage

triage_preview(con, ids, opts = NULL, overwrite_user = FALSE)

Arguments

con

Open project DB connection.

ids

Sample IDs to consider.

opts

Named list of per-rule actions; NULL reads the sample's triage_opts preset.

overwrite_user

Include units a curator decided by hand.

Value

list with, for the END STATE after Apply: n_units, n_drop, n_undecided, n_keep, n_samples, emptied, n_user_skipped, n_locked_skipped, by_rule; and, for what Apply would actually CHANGE: n_changed (units that are not skipped and whose stored triage/reason/rule differ from the proposed ones, by the same comparison auto_triage_sample() uses to decide what to write), broken down by proposed verdict into n_new_drop, n_new_keep and n_new_flag, which therefore sum to n_changed.

Details

If every rule is "off" for a sample, that sample is treated as fully skipped: the preview reports its CURRENT stored state unchanged, with zero counted in every n_new_* counter and in n_changed. See dev/design/09_TRIAGE_RULES_AND_DEPTH.md section 3.3.
